title: mFRR, manual Frequency Restoration Reserves, Capacity Market
description: Energinet makes daily procurement of manuel frequency restoration reserves (mFRR), on an hourly capacity market. This site provides market-related information for the balancing capacity market, which runs every morning. Here, you can find details on requested demand, procured volumes, and reserve prices across different directions and price areas per hour.
comment:
**Note:**
* The demand and procured volume may not match exactly. Some of the demand can be covered by other TSOs and likewise, the procured volume may help meet other TSOs’ needs. This is managed by the platform algorithm in the Nordic mFRR capacity market.  
* This dataset includes results from the daily auctions only. In DK2, additional mFRR capacity is procured in a monthly auction. For more information, see [mFRR](https://energinet.dk/el/balancering-og-systemydelser/priser-indkob-og-prognoser/).

For further information, please see: 
* [Nordic mFRR capacity market](https://nordicbalancingmodel.net/roadmap-and-projects/nordic-mfrr-capacity-market/)
* [Balancering og systemydelser](https://energinet.dk/el/balancering-og-systemydelser/)
* [Balancing and Ancillary Services](https://en.energinet.dk/electricity/balancing-and-ancillary-services/)

At November 19 2024, Denmark, Sweden, and Finland transitioned from national markets to a trilateral mFRR capacity market. The market operates on a common Nordic platform, enabling the exchange of mFRR balancing capacity across bidding zones. 

Since January 2025, mFRR capacity demand is determined daily via dynamic dimensioning based on forecasts. If forecasts underestimate the need, Energinet may initiate an extra auction to secure sufficient reserves. Results are available under: [mFRR, extra auction](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/MfrrCapacityMarketExtra). 

This dataset has data from June 2023 and is updated daily. Data before June 2023 can be found here [mFRR, Frequency Restoration Reserves manual, DK1 or mFRR, Frequency Restoration Reserves manual, DK2](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/MfrrReservesDK2).

The Upward demand and Downward demand columns contain values starting on 2024-02-28 (Time DK).

**Looking for realtime "mFRR Request"?** Find the data on [Realtime Electricity Market Data](https://www.energidataservice.dk/datasets/realtime-electricity-market).

---
**API Request Frequency** \
To get the most up-to-date data, calling the API with a dynamic timestamp such as [start=StartOfDay-P2D](https://api.energidataservice.dk/dataset/mFRRCapacityMarket?start=StartOfDay-P2D) is a good approach. Making a request every hour or so is sufficient to ensure getting the latest data.
author: Energinet

columns.description: A date and time shown in _UTC time zone_. It is the "from" timestamp for the period in which the values are valid. The dataset resolution sets the length of the interval.
columns.comment:
Please note that the _format_ shown in the example applies to data downloaded as JSON or fetched through the API.
The format is slightly different when it is shown on screen or downloaded manually as CSV or XLSX. This is mainly due to readability and consideration for Excel users.

**In preview (in the GUI)** all timestamps are shown as (display convention)
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mmZ
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00Z. 
That is without the seconds. The Z will remind viewers that this is UTC.

In **download (CSV and XLSX)** the date time are exported as
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00.
That is without the “T” and the “Z” and the seconds. Excel will recognize it as date-time. The user must remember the convention about time zones.

In **download (JSON and API)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
e.g. 2017-07-14T08:00:00.
That is without the "Z".
